title: Stop APP scams and mule accounts
question: Which payments are scams, who is behind them, and which victims should we reimburse first?
outcome: Unusual payments scored by a model, mule rings traced across victims, each case drafted by AI from the notes, call, police report and phishing screenshot, and outside records matched to customers.

steps.why: Tour the retail data: customers, transactions, fraud cases and SARs.
Score every outbound payment against the customer's own normal, so investigators see the unusual ones first.
Read the case notes, calls, police PDFs and phishing screenshots with AI SQL, and draft a reimbursement decision under the PSR rules.
Search cases and SARs in plain English, and match names on outside records to customers despite misspellings.
Mask the account identifiers investigators don't need, before any of this reaches an agent or app.
Protect names, dates of birth, incomes and case notes by what they are, so analysts see banded values and nobody sees what they should not.
Catalogue the police reports and phishing screenshots on the stage, and share one case folder with the reviewing team only.

title: Keep the customers worth keeping
question: Who is about to leave, why, and where would closing a branch push more of them out?
outcome: An attrition model in the Model Registry scoring every customer, each customer's lifetime value and value at risk with a next-best offer, the reasons behind each score, what customers say on calls, and the profit at risk if each branch closed.

steps.why: Tour the retail data: monthly profit per customer, products, branches and calls.
Learn the label, point-in-time features and the leakage traps before training anything.
Train, track and register an attrition model, then score every customer.
Calibrate the attrition model into real probabilities and predict each customer's margin, tracked and registered.
Turn the predictions into lifetime value and value at risk, rank the save list by money, and pick a next-best offer.
Compare every branch, neighbourhood and value segment with its city and the UK using level of detail metrics in a semantic view, then ask an agent.
Which branches could close, which nearby branches absorb their customers, and how much longer each customer travels.
Advanced: turn a real-roads drive-time matrix into the closure lookup behind the demo, and see why hexagon size matters.
Find the reasons in customers' own words: savings rates, branch access, service.

title: Compare every branch with its city and the UK
question: Which branches and neighbourhoods are worth more or less than their city, and how much of the UK's value at risk sits in each?
outcome: One semantic view with level of detail metrics, so every branch is compared with its city and the UK the same way in SQL, Semantic Studio, CoWork and Power BI.

steps.why: Tour the retail data: customers, branches and monthly profit.
Calibrated attrition and margin predictions for every customer.
Lifetime value and value at risk per customer, by segment.
Compare each branch and neighbourhood with its city and the UK in one semantic view, then ask an agent.

title: Corporate client 360 and payment operations
question: Which clients' payments are failing or running slow, what are they telling us, and what should ops do next?
outcome: Tested, self-refreshing payment data products, a client 360 report and agent for relationship managers, alert triage with AI next actions, and feedback themed by AI SQL.

steps.why: Explore the corporate payments data product end to end.
Build tested, documented dbt models from the Iceberg sources.
A live client 360 report ops and RMs filter themselves, refreshed every morning.
One trusted definition of a client's payments health that anyone can question in plain English.
A client 360 agent relationship managers can ask about their own clients.
Triage operations alerts and let AI suggest the next action.
Theme and score every piece of client feedback with AI SQL.

title: Roll out AI safely
question: How do we give every team AI on bank data without losing control of PII, access or audit?
outcome: PII classified, tagged and masked; lineage and access history that prove who saw what; and every AI client governed through one gateway, with agents built on governed data only.

steps.why: See the data products the AI will sit on.
Classify, tag, mask and filter PII once, so it's enforced in every tool, agent and app.
Build an agent whose tools answer from governed data, not from whatever it can reach.
One masking policy per kind of data, attached to the personal data tag, so a new column is protected the moment it is tagged.
Prove lineage and who accessed what, for audit.
One inventory of every stage and registered model, with its owner and who can read it.
Govern every AI client and model through one gateway.

title: Prove control to the regulator
question: Could we show a regulator, today, that we stay inside impact tolerance, answer data requests on time and know every model we run?
outcome: An impact tolerance alert that escalates breaches with its own history, a customer's data request answered from tagged personal data with who read it, and a model risk evidence pack from the Model Registry. Each control leaves the evidence behind.

steps.why: Operational resilience: hold each important business service's impact tolerance as data and escalate a breach with a Snowflake Alert.
Classify, tag and mask personal data once, so the policies follow it everywhere.
UK GDPR: answer a customer's request for their data from the tags, hold back financial crime records, log the due date.
Show the regulator that every personal column is masked by role, with a coverage report that lists any gap.
Prove who accessed what, from access history.
Show every model and evidence file the bank holds, who owns it and who can read it.
A calibrated challenger to the attrition model, and a margin model with its baseline: evidence for model risk review.
Model risk: inventory, validation against real outcomes, champion vs challenger, model card and approval.
APP scams and SARs: draft reimbursement decisions and check SAR narratives, with people deciding.

title: Prove vulnerable customers get as good an outcome
question: Do customers in vulnerable circumstances get outcomes as good as everyone else's, and where they don't, why not?
outcome: Vulnerability cues read from every call by AI SQL, similar calls found with Cortex Search, value and offers checked for fair value, and the personal data behind it masked by role, so outcomes can be compared without exposing anyone.

steps.why: Tour the retail data: the vulnerable customers register, complaints with redress paid, calls and churn.
Read every call transcript with AI SQL: sentiment, reason and vulnerability cues, plus the facts in each complaint.
Find every call like this one in plain English, so a cue spotted once is found everywhere.
Value at risk and next best offers by segment: check what vulnerable customers are offered is fair value.
Mask names, incomes and complaint text by role, so outcomes can be monitored without exposing the people behind them.

whyNow.text: The FCA and ICO expect firms to monitor whether customers in vulnerable circumstances get worse outcomes than others, find the root cause and act.

source.label: Joint FCA and ICO statement on vulnerability related data

whyNow.text: Indicators of vulnerability can appear in customer interactions and transaction data, and data protection law does not stop firms acting on them lawfully.

source.label: Joint FCA and ICO statement on vulnerability related data

title: Be ready to report an operational incident
question: If payments fail tomorrow, would we spot it in time, know which clients were hurt and have the evidence a regulator's incident report asks for?
outcome: A dynamic table that keeps the SLA monitor fresh with tested data, impact tolerance breaches escalated by a Snowflake Alert with their own history, AI-ranked alerts linked to unhappy clients, and lineage and access history to show what was affected and who looked.

steps.why: Keep the payments SLA monitor fresh with a dynamic table, and prove the data feeding it passes quality checks.
Hold each important business service's impact tolerance as data, and escalate a breach with a Snowflake Alert that records it.
Rank open alerts with AI next actions and link them to the clients complaining, to size the harm.
Lineage shows what an incident touched downstream; access history shows who read the client data.

whyNow.text: New FCA, PRA and Bank of England operational incident reporting rules come into force on 18 March 2027, with one form for every regulator.
An incident must be reported if it risks intolerable consumer harm, the safety and soundness of the firm, or market stability and confidence.
The PRA keeps operational resilience and data risk among its 2026 priorities for UK banks and building societies.

source.label: Bank of England: UK deposit takers, 2026 priorities
